svg.data-vd-steps: [[0, "How vaccination protects a whole population."], [1, "One infected person enters each population."], [3, "Without immunity, the infection spreads to almost everyone."], [7, "With some immunity, it still spreads, but more slowly."], [11, "With high vaccination coverage, chains of transmission break: herd immunity protects the unvaccinated."]]
svg.title: Herd immunity
svg.desc: Three populations of 48 people with no, some and most people immune; one infected person enters each and infection spreads widely, partly, or is stopped by herd immunity.
svg.text: A simplified model: each infected person can infect neighbours who are not immune.

g.data-info: Each infected person passes the infection to several others, so it spreads quickly through the population.
Immune people block some routes; the infection still spreads.
When most people are immune, an infected person rarely meets anyone susceptible: chains of transmission break, protecting people who cannot be vaccinated (babies, people with weak immune systems).
